newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar eases, topside heavy vs yen in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar eases, topside heavy vs yen in Tokyo.

text.p: *Dollar eases slightly against yen in morning Tokyo after earlier rising on short-covering and commercial buying at local fixing at 0100 GMT.
*Dollar topside remains heavy due to exporter offers near 114.80 yen and above.
*President Clinton voiced concern about Japan's rising trade surplus at meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Hashimoto, but impact was limited as he made similar comments overnight.
*In meeting with Hashimoto, Clinton also stressed importance of Japan promoting domestic demand-led growth and deregulation of economy.
*"He (U.S. President Bill Clinton) voiced specific concerns," White House aide Daniel Tarullo told reporters in Denver.

*White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Clinton also pointedly reminded Hashimoto that previous persistent Japanese trade surpluses had been source of "real damage to the bilateral relationship" and said the two nations should not allow trade to become dominant factor in bilateral ties.
*"Basically, his comments were not that fresh compared with those overnight," a trust bank dealer said.
*One city bank dealer said issue of Japan's growing trade surplus will be less of focus in currency markets now, after digesting slew of comments overnight and Friday morning.
*"I think the Group of Seven (G7) summit will not talk about Japan's trade surplus as a major issue. Now the market is awaiting the BOJ 'tankan' report next week," he added.
*Bank of Japan's key quarterly "tankan" corporate survey is due on June 25.
*Dollar rose against yen in early Tokyo mainly due to short-covering, which was encouraged by remarks by U.S. President Bill Clinton, market sources said.

*Clinton, in White House interview recorded for Japanese television before departing for Denver on Thursday, said he was concerned about Japan's large surplus with the United States but added that exchange rates should not be used to correct trade imbalances.
